[h1]Einstieg[/h1]
„9 Clues 2 - The Ward“ ist klassisches Wimmelbild-Futter für zwischendurch. Wer Lust auf Mystery, etwas Psycho-Vibe und entspannte Rätsel hat, bekommt hier solide Genre-Kost ohne große Überraschungen.

[h1]Handlung / Story[/h1]
Die Story dreht sich um ein altes Sanatorium, dunkle Experimente und eine Vergangenheit, die besser begraben geblieben wäre. Viel wird über Notizen, Rückblenden und Dialoge erzählt. Die Handlung ist nicht mega komplex, funktioniert aber gut genug, um dran zu bleiben. Gruselig eher auf Atmosphäre als auf Jumpscare-Basis.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Typisches Wimmelbild-Gameplay: Suchbilder, Minigames, Inventarrätsel. Alles bekannt, alles solide umgesetzt. Die Rätsel sind logisch, selten frustrierend und gut in den Spielfluss eingebettet. Große Innovationen gibt es nicht, aber das Rad will das Spiel auch nicht neu erfinden.

[h1]Schwierigkeit[/h1]
Der Schwierigkeitsgrad ist eher locker. Vieles erklärt sich von selbst, Hinweise sind jederzeit verfügbar. Ideal zum Abschalten nach einem langen Tag, weniger für Rätsel-Masochist*innen. Ich fand das angenehm entspannt.

[h1]Grafik[/h1]
Die Hintergründe sind detailreich und schön düster gestaltet. Das Sanatorium wirkt glaubwürdig heruntergekommen und leicht unheimlich. Die Wimmelbilder sind übersichtlich und nicht unnötig überladen. Technisch kein Highlight, stilistisch aber stimmig.

[h1]Sound[/h1]
Der Soundtrack unterstützt die Atmosphäre gut, bleibt aber eher im Hintergrund. Dezente Musik, passende Geräusche, keine nervigen Loops. Die Sprachausgabe ist okay, aber kein Must-have.

[h1]Technik / Bugs[/h1]
Technisch lief bei mir alles sauber. Keine Abstürze, keine Gamebreaker. Übergänge und Ladezeiten sind unauffällig. Genauso, wie man es von einem Genre-Vertreter erwartet.

[h1]Grind[/h1]
Grind gibt es quasi nicht. Wer möchte, kann optionale Sammelobjekte mitnehmen, muss aber nicht. Kein künstliches Strecken, kein unnötiges Backtracking.

[h1]Spielzeit[/h1]
Die Spielzeit liegt bei ca. 3 bis 4 Stunden. Perfekt für ein Wochenende oder ein paar entspannte Abende. Nicht zu kurz, nicht zu lang. Ich habe für zwei komplette Durchläufe knappe 6 Stunden gebraucht.

[h1]Errungenschaften / Achievements[/h1]
Die Achievements sind größtenteils straightforward. Vieles bekommt man automatisch, anderes durch gründliches Spielen. Wie üblich bei den Wimmelbildgames von Artifex Mundi gibt es Errungenschaften wie z. B. „Drei Rätsel ohne Überspringen zu lösen“ oder „Bewältige fünf Wimmelbild-Rätsel jeweils unter 2 Minuten“. Leider sind 2 Durchläufe notwendig - einmal alle Wimmelbilder meistern und ein anderes Mal alle Mahjong-Spiele zu meistern, um 100 % zu erzielen. Kein harter Grind, aber auch keine besonderen Herausforderungen.

[h1]Preis[/h1]
Ich habe „9 Clues 2 - The Ward“ für 2,58 € am 07.07.2025 gekauft.

[h1]Fazit[/h1]
„9 Clues 2 - The Ward“ ist ein solides Wimmelbild-Adventure mit düsterer Atmosphäre und entspannter Schwierigkeit. Keine großen Überraschungen, aber genau das, was das Genre verspricht. Ideal für Fans von Mystery-Wimmelbildern oder als chilliges Spiel für zwischendurch. Kein Meisterwerk, aber absolut okay.

[hr]Die Rezension spiegelt [u]meine ganz persönliche Meinung[/u] zu „9 Clues 2 - The Ward“ wider. Habt ihr inhaltliche, grammatikalische oder Rechtschreibfehler bemerkt oder habe ich etwas übersehen, bin ich euch für einen Hinweis dankbar.[/hr]

Although this game is the sequel to 9 Clues: The Secret of Serpent Creek, I don't think it's a direct sequel. The voice actress for the main character sounds different to me, and while they are both investigators, in the first game the character seemed like a private investigator versus in this game where the main character seems more like an official police officer.

This isn't necessarily a bad thing though. The style of gameplay is incredibly similar with the first game's signature "reconstruction" scenes where you have to pick out parts of a scene to piece together what happened, as well as the usual finding and using items and looking through hidden object scene to find key items to progress.

The story was fine, it's more geared towards a mystery just like the first one with strange events happening and you trying to determine what is happening and only really getting the final answer at the end of the game. One thing I did appreciate too is that even though this is at an asylum, the game doesn't just depict all of the inmates as violent and dangerous, which is an old "insane person" trope I don't really care for. And most of the game is spent moving through different areas of the asylum and getting access to more and more of it as you play.

The puzzles were fine, not the most challenging ones I've seen in a game like this, but they were fine enough and intuitive to figure out. The hidden object scene were also fine without a lot of egregiously hard to find items, just an even pace all the way through.

There are collectibles in the game, and they were fun to find and probably the thing I felt was the most challenging at times since there are multiple types of collectibles to be on the look out for. I missed [i]one[/i] item in my first playthrough and had to do another to mop it up, which was fine because you have to play through twice because there is once achievement for completing all of the hidden object puzzles and one for completing all of the Mahjong games.

This game offers Mahjong instead of hidden object games you can play instead of doing the hidden object puzzles. And I like both, so I had no issues with this, but I have to mention that when I was playing this game I saw a note in the community section about a bug where the game would have a bug that would prevent you from selecting Mahjong games if you switch back and play the first game as a hidden object puzzle or something. I took the advice of that post and played the first game as Mahjong and then the rest as hidden object puzzles. Then for my second playthrough I played a hidden object game as the first one and the rest as Mahjong to finish the achievements. This worked for me, though I have no idea if it was necessary. But if you're having trouble with those I would advise trying this method.

Even though other people reported the Mahjong game issue, I didn't have any technical issues with the game. There are collectibles in the game, but there is no bonus adventure.

9 Clues 2: The Ward is an underwhelming hidden object adventure published by Artifex Mundi, set in an insane asylum where a murder case took place. I did not enjoy it.

There are some great and gorgeous Artifex Mundi hidden object games out there, particularly some of those not just published but also developed by them. This is not one of those games. Art and animations look incredibly dated, and would've already done so back in 2015 when the game was released.

Voice acting and writing are also bad. Most damningly, the protagonist is such a lousy detective that she gets incapacitated several times by antagonists. Not every game needs to be a power fantasy, but in this game the protagonist is handed the Idiot Ball any time a cutscene appears. I didn't like the finale, either. 

The gameplay itself doesn't work, either. You get the typical hidden object slop where you're tasked to find generic reused assets that are low contrast and don't fit the game theme. Also, the hidden object puzzles here ask you to find items by name (e.g. "bow"), rather than by shape, and this just doesn't work, like when it turns out that the requested item is a knotted ribbon, rather than the weapon you use to shoot arrows. Due to such poor design, my playtime was mostly spent spam-clicking everywhere. Yuck.

Finally, the Steam achievements are implemented in a really lousy way: a whole bunch of them are missable, and the game doesn't support backtracking at all, so 100%ing this thoroughly underwhelming game would require multiple playthroughs.

Not recommended. Play a good hidden object game instead. I'm partial to Artifex Mundi's [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/284850/Grim_Legends_The_Forsaken_Bride/]Grim Legends: The Forsaken Bride[/url], for example.

[h2] Solve the Mystery of Mnemosyne Asylum and Learn Its Secrets [/h2]
It’s been a bit since I last played a hidden object adventure game and since I played the original game in the [i]9 Clues[/i] series. I remember having a lot of fun playing [i]The Secret of Serpent Creek[/i], so I thought I’d finally check out the sequel. Time for another mystery!

Stepping back into the shoes of the young detective from the first game, we receive a call from a distressed individual who asks us to come to Mnemosyne Asylum, which stands alone, isolated on an island. With the help of our new partner (Owen Duffer from the first game), we head there to start our investigation. But, once we arrive, a doctor falls from a window to his untimely demise. Something very strange is going on at Mnemosyne. What secrets are the residents and employees of the institution hiding? Who is Ginger? Can the mystery be solved before disaster strikes the asylum once more?

I wanted to play a hidden object game again, so I thought this one would be a good choice, and I also wanted to continue the [i]9 Clues[/i] series. To be honest, I slightly enjoyed this game more than the first one. What I really liked more about this one was its story and how creepier it was. Throughout the game, the puzzles and hidden object scenes were well-balanced. While there weren’t many HO scenes in the beginning, they picked up later in the game. The only real puzzle that I had issues with was when I had to move gears to their correct positions near the end. Just like the first game, you are looking for nine clues relating to the mystery and a Detective Mode for crime scenes to reconstruct what happened returned. Like [i]Serpent Creek[/i], this one was also a pretty casual experience overall.

I do wish this game had gotten another sequel, as it would’ve been nice to see the two detectives again, but this wasn’t a bad end to the series.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Я не грав у другу частину і тому не можу сказати чи повʼязана з нею друга в чому я сильно сумніваюсь. 

Ми граємо за молоду детективесу, яка приїхала за викликом в дурку. Що правда якби вона прибула трохи раніше, то можливо встигла врятувати того, хто дзвонив. І тепер наша ціль дійти до зловмисника та зупинити його.

Тут нема розслідування як такого, не треба гадати, хто може ховатися за маскою опудала. Гра доволі швидко викладає карти на стіл і все що залишає це просто вирішувати місцеві загадки в дусі знайди усі предмети, склади пазли і навіть маджонг. 

В грі можна зустріти некритичні візуальні баги, де в деяких персонажів зникає голова. Однак не забувайте де відбуваються події гри. 

З приємного можу відзначити візуальний стиль. Він простий і доволі приємний. Обличчя персонажів рухаються від чого можна зловити ефект лиховісної долини. В тим гра коштує не так багато і очікувати від гри жанру наведи та натисни якихось крутих ефектів не варто.

Гра доволі коротка і для отримання усіх досягнень мені знадобились трохи менше шести годин, а це два проходження. 

Я впевнений є більш вдалі проекти, можливо навіть цього видавця, але для 2024 року гра вже застаріла і щоб виправити ситуацію і б рекомендував поєднувати декілька жанрів та не боятися експериментів замість того щоб випускати десятки однакових проектів, де левову частину робити роблять художники.
